opportunity: coreutils fmt -O2 calls one static function three times from main and kuna renders one, two and three arguments; the three-argument site reads two `// rdx` locals nothing assigns. The callee's own recovered prototype takes two parameters. `argclobber` fixed that in #652 but shipped OFF, because the only clause that could speak for the callee was a bounded walk of its entry, and four ordinary programs hide a real read from that walk (a jump table, the walk's instruction budget, a PLT import, a 16-byte rax:rdx struct return forwarded onward). With protoorder (#669) merged the callee's own RECOVERED prototype is readable at the call site, and it separates every shipped drop from every counterexample.
inspiration: coreutils fmt -O2 main 0x26a0 -> fmt 0x3700 at 0x2ac1; upstream ParamListStandardOut::fillinMap (fspec.cc:1721) and AncestorRealistic::enterNode (funcdata_varnode.cc:2043)

rule_change.admits: the callee's RECOVERED prototype (stated by `protoorder types`) exists for this entry, has no parameter overlapping the argument's register bytes, AND accounts -- storage for storage -- for every argument the drop leaves behind
rule_change.vetoes: unchanged caller-side clauses, plus TWO readings of the callee's body from the per-image entry-liveness summary: `proves_input` (the bounded entry walk positively sees the register READ before it is written) and `resolve_forward_transfer` (the callee must have WRITTEN the register before every control transfer that cannot be answered for -- CALLIND, BRANCHIND, CALLOTHER, an indexed register-file LOAD/STORE, an undecodable instruction, and a direct CALL whose target carries neither a declared non-variadic prototype nor a body that answers the same question of itself, recursively, within a 32-body budget). Naming a target is not accounting for it: an import's PLT stub jumps through its GOT slot and answers nothing. Neither reading can admit a drop.
inert_where: kuna decompile (one function per forked process)
rule_change.value_naming: `on` now means the new rule; no `proto` value was added, because the old rule is unsound where they differ and identical where they do not
rule_change.why_the_accounting_clause: a recovery SHORT of what the call passes is not a statement that the tail is unwanted but a statement that the recovery did not reach the tail. A forwarding thunk (`mov (%rdi),%rax; jmp *%rax`) recovers one parameter while the function it tail calls consumes three, and protoorder states that short list in BOTH its modes; the free-bytes test alone deleted the forwarded argument. ce-forward-thunk.{c,s}
rule_change.protoorder_does_not_decline_a_variadic: Decline::UnderRecovered and Decline::RegisterFileFull live in park_recovered's LOCK branch; the default `types` mode returns through state_recovered_types before them. Decline::Variadic is only ever set from a declared `...`, which Decline::Declared rejects one branch earlier, so it cannot fire on a stripped image. Measured: `long vlog(int,long,...)` with a va_arg read, gcc -O2 stripped, prints `[protoorder] state sub_11d0 params=3` under KUNA_PROTOORDER_TRACE=1. What declines the drop at a stripped variadic is the recovered list itself -- a register-save prologue reads every argument register, so the list carries the one the drop would take.
rule_change.why_the_forwarding_clause: a recovered prototype states what a callee NAMES. `long fwd(struct box*o,long a,long b){ if(!a) return 0; return o->fn(o,a,b); }` compiles under gcc -O2 to `test %rsi,%rsi; je; jmp *(%rdi)`, recovering exactly the TWO parameters a drop would leave behind -- so the accounting clause is satisfied and the forwarded third argument was deleted along with the preceding call's rax:rdx return half. At the `jmp` rdx is unwritten, and that is what declines it. The same is true with no pointer anywhere: `long wrap(void*o,long a,long b){ if(!a) return 0; return ext3(o,a,b); }` with ext3 an unsignatured import recovers the same two parameters, and the direct call is declined only because its target cannot answer for rdx (ce-import-forward.c; ce-forward-thunk-2frame.c is the pointer one an ordinary call frame deeper). An incomplete summary (probe budget, runaway written set) declines too, which subsumes ce-probe-budget a second, independent way.

programs: ce-forward-thunk.c + ce-forward-thunk.s (indirect tail call; recovers 1 parameter, forwards 3)
ce-forward-thunk-2param.c -- a 2-parameter forwarding thunk in plain C (no hand asm); declined by the forwarding walk, NOT by the prototype

ce-forward-thunk-2frame.c -- ce-forward-thunk-2param one ordinary direct call frame deeper
